The identity of the submitter is irrelevant, the content of the submission is what matters. I don't know if any of you have spent any time as a troll, but a troll looks for the most appealing bait and then sees if they can get anyone to bite. The focus isn't on creating a lie, the focus is on getting a bite - eliciting an emotional reaction from someone.

The proper way of disarming a concern troll is to dispassionately scrutinize what they actually say and disregard the way that they say it. Dispassionate scrutiny is also the best way to evaluate issues raised by people who legitimately care about voat and determine whether those issues are problems, and to evaluate whether people are overreacting to something that is not a problem. Dispassionate scrutiny is also the best way to identify and evaluate the effectiveness of any solutions to address problems.

If you agree that dispassionate scrutiny is the proper response in all those situations, then it doesn't matter whether someone is a concern troll or legit. Furthermore, it's possible for someone whose intention is to troll to select bait that actually is a problem that should be addressed by people who legitimately care about this site. The most effective trolling has a nugget of truth in it somewhere, and that nugget of truth can have value regardless of the intentions of the troll.

I don't see the value in having an individual call-out and intervention for a particular person like this. The bottom line is that they are identifying an issue that may be of concern, you respond according to whether you agree

  • If someone is alarmed by something and you are not alarmed by that thing, then do not upvoat their post.

  • If their "raise the alarm" post seems to be lying and exaggerating in order to draw attention to that thing, then downvoat their post.

  • If you are unsure if you should be alarmed, then post in the comments section to ask questions about what they find so alarming. Discuss whether something is an overreaction or if measures are already in place that will prevent the thing that they find so alarming.

  • If you are also alarmed by the thing that they are alarmed by, then upvoat the post and discuss the potential implications of that thing in the comments section. Discuss possible solutions, the potential flaws or harm that could come from those solutions, and attempt to identify solutions that would be most effective in preserving the health, openness, and the principle of free speech on voat.
